result.scope: Traced the FCDP drafting protocol end-to-end in archon-cli — from `archon evidence curate` / the `archon draft` wizard through pack assembly, the draft-time bank gate, the D1→D1.5→D2→gauntlet→R-loop orchestrator, «Qnn» substitution, and the post-run provenance import — naming every function and recording what provenance is carried and dropped at each hop. Read crates/archon-draft in full (src/{lib,fable,gauntlet,judge,orchestrator,provenance}.rs, src/bin/archon_fcdp.rs, tests/{golden,orchestrator}.rs, tests/fixtures/m6/*), crates/archon-evidence/src/{lib,pack,verify,quote_trim,index}.rs, src/command/{curate,curate_agent,evidence,draft}.rs, crates/archon-docs/src/quote_verify.rs, plus plans/fable-console-drafting-protocol-v2.md and both plans/fcdp-archon-port-plan*.md. Ran read-only `archon docs verify-quote` and `archon evidence find` (with and without --index) against the live 942 MB store. This agent establishes the VALUE side only; I did not re-audit the incumbent compiler/runtime beyond confirming whether an FCDP implementation exists there.
result.summary:
The user's statement that "the FCDP drafting protocol pulls its quotations from archon" is literally true and stronger than stated: FCDP has NO implementation in claudeflow-testing at all. The only FCDP artifact there is the 43-line scripts/substitute-quote-ids.py plus the plan documents; `find . -name "*.py" | grep -iE "fcdp|gauntlet|judge"` returns nothing else. The entire gate-enforced pipeline — pack schema, G-P, «Qnn» substitution, the seven-gate gauntlet, the G-E/G-G judges, the R-loop, the hash chain, the disclosure declaration — is 3,686 lines of Rust in crates/archon-draft, driven from src/command/draft.rs. Quotations reach a draft through exactly one path: assemble_pack (pack.rs:72) → trim_to_relevant_span (pack.rs:92) → reanchor_cites (pack.rs:165) → write_pack (pack.rs:236) → preflight_draft_inputs/verify_bank (draft.rs:972, verify.rs:130) → orchestrator::run (orchestrator.rs:412) → substitute_quote_ids (draft lib.rs:246), which is the single hop where quoted words enter the prose.

All three assertions are CONFIRMED. QuoteEntry is exactly `{text, cite}` (draft lib.rs:169-173) — no chunk_id, no offsets, no bbox, no match_kind. Verification is `{quotes_verified_at: String, verified_against: Vec<String>, test_fixture: bool}` (lib.rs:158-166); in the real m6 pack `verified_against` holds two free-text notes naming PDF paths and extraction method — nothing machine-checks them. gp_validate (lib.rs:178-234) takes no db handle and never touches the corpus: it checks P4a↔P4b id bijection, non-empty text/evidence/locks/usage, and `quotes_verified_at == today`. One important CORRECTION to the framing: gp_validate is not the only gate on the drafting path. `archon draft` runs preflight_draft_inputs (draft.rs:972), which calls archon_evidence::verify_bank and BLOCKS the run on any non-Exact status including NearVerbatim (verify.rs:88-101, H-9). So a content re-check against the live corpus DOES exist today — it is just not in gp_validate, it is skipped for test_fixture packs, it degrades to a warning when the corpus is absent (draft.rs ~1046), and the standalone archon-fcdp binary bypasses it entirely (bin/archon_fcdp.rs:116-173).

The provenance loss is severe and is a pure field-width problem, not a missing-capability problem. quote_verify computes exact char offsets (a,b) at quote_verify.rs:167-170, threads them into build_location's local_of closure to narrow page and bbox, then discards them because QuoteFragment (quote_verify.rs:33-42) has no offset field. curate.rs:44 then collapses the whole QuoteLocation into a ReviewItem, dropping the FragmentLocator (the Bekker number — the citation-grade locus) entirely and reducing similarity to the string "exact-1.00" or "fuzzy". curate.rs:174-215 then drops bbox, chunk_id and page_boxes, hardcodes `intended_use: "evidential grounding"`, and writes the RA's one-line claim into BOTH `description` and `evidence` — so G-E item E4 ("Is each quotation used in a way consistent with its stated intended rhetorical use?", judge.rs:54) judges every RA-curated pack against a constant. The RA's per-quote `rationale` reaches stdout (evidence.rs:343) and the --json dump (evidence.rs:401) and nothing else. By the time the pack is on disk, a quote is two strings.

The value of a claim-level index living in archon is demonstrable rather than theoretical, and the live run shows it exactly. `archon evidence find "rhetorical incorporation"` returns 10/10 candidates from Bitzer's "The Rhetorical Situation", every one OCR-corrupted ("pnractical", "consiaered", "moditication"), none about incorporation. With `--index` the compiled index matches the concept "Incorporation" and work-boosts Calleja's In-Game into the top two slots — but the chunks it surfaces are "mimetic control" (p.64, provenance unresolved) and "macro Involvernent" (p.38). The work-level index gets the right BOOK and cannot get the right SENTENCE. Meanwhile the m6 pack's Q1 — the definitional passage — verifies live at exact-1.00, p.169, bbox [58,365,375,487]. A human found that sentence; the pipeline cannot. That gap is precisely what claim-level granularity closes, and archon already owns both halves it would connect: the index consumer (archon-evidence/src/index.rs, 977 lines, already reading compiled-index.json) and the span prover (quote_verify, already returning sub-span-resolved page and bbox).

Concretely, a claim-level index in archon lets a pack carry what it cannot today: QuoteEntry widened with {document_id, chunk_id, char_start, char_end, page, bbox, match_kind, similarity} — every field already computed and thrown away; a typed FragmentLocator instead of a formatted locus string; real per-claim intended_use and distinct description/evidence instead of one duplicated note; index tension-edge material bound to the specific claim for D1.5's counterargument pass (today TensionEdge and Hook are parsed at index.rs:71-100 and used only for query expansion — build_head and d15_prompt carry none of it); and content hashes from doc_chunk_hashes instead of free-text verification notes. It also enables four gates that cannot run today: (1) offset-anchored re-verification, which catches the case that currently passes silently — the quote is verbatim somewhere in the cited document but not at the passage it was curated from, because find_fragment_bboxes takes the FIRST exact substring match (quote_verify.rs:167) and cannot tell "my sentence" from "the same words 300 pages later"; (2) a mechanical claim-fidelity check, replacing part of the LLM-judged E2/E3/E5 battery whose truncation failure mode is documented as L7 in the port plan; (3) a cleaning-version/re-ingest staleness gate keyed on raw_sha256 rather than a calendar date; (4) a coverage gate over contested claims, so "every weakness" is checkable rather than detected by substring-searching the model's own skeleton for "SURFACE-TO-USER" (orchestrator.rs:484).

Building the overhaul in claudeflow-testing means building a second copy of the index consumer and a second copy of the span prover, in a repo whose .archon store is 28 KB and empty, to feed a drafting protocol that does not exist there. The honest counterweight is corpus quality, not architecture: the Bitzer hits show heavy OCR corruption and `has_bbox` was false on every one of them, so 450,000 clause records extracted over that text will inherit the corruption, and claim records must tolerate bbox:None.

findings.claim: The FCDP drafting protocol has NO implementation in claudeflow-testing. The only FCDP code there is a 43-line substitution script; the whole gate-enforced pipeline exists solely in archon-cli. The user's premise is therefore not merely true but understated.

By contrast /home/dalton/projects/archon-cli/crates/archon-draft = 3,686 lines across src/{lib,fable,gauntlet,judge,orchestrator,provenance}.rs + bin + tests.

Its complete checks: P4a-empty-but-bank-nonempty, P4a id present in bank, bank id present in P4a, non-empty quote text, non-empty P5 content, non-empty P3 locks, non-empty P9 usage, non-empty P7 (warn), unapproved exemplars (warn), quotes_verified_at == today. findings.claim: CORRECTION to the established facts: a content re-check against the live corpus DOES exist on the `archon draft` path — it is just not in gp_validate. verify_bank blocks the run on any non-Exact status, including NearVerbatim ≥0.9.

result.port_cost:
Two separable costs; I size the first two and refuse to invent the third.

(1) THREADING PROVENANCE THROUGH THE EXISTING PACK PATH — 300-500 lines across 5 structs in 5 files, plus golden-fixture regeneration. Add {char_start, char_end} to QuoteFragment (crates/archon-docs/src/quote_verify.rs:33-42, values already computed at :167-170), stop discarding FragmentLocator and similarity at src/command/curate.rs:44-107, carry chunk_id/bbox/document_id through CuratedQuote (crates/archon-evidence/src/pack.rs:20-41, which already carries document_id), widen QuoteEntry (crates/archon-draft/src/lib.rs:169-173) additively with #[serde(default)]. BASIS: commit 4c581761 "feat(evidence): Pack assembly" = 250 insertions / 4 files; commit 3e689c7f "bank re-verification" = 298 insertions / 4 files; commit ac7bd3b4 "trim pack quotes to claim-relevant sentence spans" = 387 insertions / 5 files. This work is the same shape and scale as all three. Add fixture cost: provenance.rs declare() output is byte-asserted (tests/golden.rs:169-188) and five gauntlet reference JSONs are equality-checked (golden.rs:55-125).

(2) CLAIM-LEVEL STORE + READER + QUERY SURFACE IN ARCHON — 900-1,400 lines. BASIS: commit 6cd6691a "feat(evidence): compiled research index — canonical expansion, owning-work routing, tension surfacing" = 857 insertions / 6 files delivered the directly analogous reader-plus-routing layer (now 977 lines at crates/archon-evidence/src/index.rs), and crates/archon-docs/src/schema.rs is the in-repo precedent for a CozoDB relation module. Add ~150-250 lines to thread claim/tension material into build_head and d15_prompt (orchestrator.rs:67, :127), on the additive-Pack-field precedent set by DraftType (lib.rs:45-64, :48 serde default, round-trip test at :652).

(3) CLAIM EXTRACTION AT 45,000-CLAIM / 450,000-CLAUSE SCALE — NO ESTIMATE. Nothing in archon-cli extracts claims or clauses today; ingestion produces chunks, blocks, page breaks and locators only. No commit in this repo is comparable, so any number I gave would be invented. What I can say with evidence: this cost is repo-independent — it is new work whether it lands in Rust or in Python — so it does not discriminate between the two hosts. What DOES discriminate is that building it in claudeflow-testing additionally requires re-implementing (1) and (2), i.e. a second copy of the index consumer (977 lines already written in Rust) and a second copy of the span prover (crates/archon-docs/src/quote_verify.rs, backed by a 942 MB store with 224 documents), to feed a drafting protocol that has no implementation in that repo at all.
risks: Corpus text quality is the binding constraint, not architecture. Live `archon evidence find` output shows heavy OCR corruption in the ingested text ('pnractical', 'consiaered in 1tsely', 'moditication', 'Involvernent') and one candidate that failed to re-anchor at all. Extracting 450,000 clause records over that text manufactures false clauses at scale, and a claim-level index inherits every corruption. This risk is identical in either repo but is amplified by clause granularity — a chunk-level system tolerates a few corrupted tokens; a clause-level system indexes them as claims.

bbox provenance is not universal. Every Bitzer hit and the Calleja p.38 hit reported 'no bbox'; quote_verify.rs:36 documents bbox as None on the pdftotext path. Claim records must tolerate bbox:None, and any gate keyed on bbox presence will fail-closed on a large fraction of the corpus.

Format-parity tests pin the current pack and provenance serialization. crates/archon-draft/src/provenance.rs:9-10 states the byte-exact Python json.dumps reproduction is what lets Rust verify a Python-written chain, asserted against the real 19-record M6 chain (tests/golden.rs:154); declare() output is asserted by equality (golden.rs:169-188). Additive #[serde(default)] fields keep old packs READING, but any change to what is WRITTEN breaks byte-parity. Fixtures must be regenerated deliberately, with the old chain retained.

Two entry points to the drafting engine, only one gated. src/command/draft.rs:789 runs preflight_draft_inputs/verify_bank; crates/archon-draft/src/bin/archon_fcdp.rs:116-173 runs the orchestrator directly with no verification. A new claim-level gate wired only into the first inherits the same split.

REPORT_FLOOR = 0.60 (quote_verify.rs:20) means find_fragment_bboxes returns Some() for a fabricated quote. The existing gate is correct because it keys on MatchKind (verify.rs:196-204, :88-101), but that correctness is a convention, not a type-level guarantee — a new gate testing Option::is_some() would silently pass fabrications.

The curation bridge is where provenance dies, and it is easy to leave behind. src/command/curate.rs:204-211 hardcodes intended_use, duplicates the note into description and evidence, and derives EvidenceGrade from a display string prefix. If claim records land in the store but curate.rs is not changed with them, packs keep carrying the constant 'evidential grounding' and G-E item E4 keeps judging against nothing.

Preflight degrades to a warning rather than blocking when the corpus DB is unavailable or empty (src/command/draft.rs ~1046, D8). A machine without the 942 MB store drafts unverified with a console warning. Any claim-level gate must decide deliberately whether to inherit that fail-open posture.

The compiled index is a pre-compiled snapshot (documented at crates/archon-evidence/src/index.rs:17-18: 'recompile on reingest or routing goes stale'). A claim-level index over 224 documents makes staleness a much larger correctness surface, and archon has no staleness check today — quotes_verified_at (lib.rs:222) compares a date against today, which detects elapsed time, not a changed source. doc_chunk_hashes {raw_sha256, cleaning_version, commit_hash} exists in schema.rs to fix this but nothing references it from a pack.

Scope discipline. Landing claim records in archon does NOT by itself improve retrieval — discover() would need the claim layer wired into ranking (crates/archon-evidence/src/lib.rs:126-389), and the drafting prompts would need new P-fields. A partial port that stores claims without wiring them buys nothing and adds a second index to keep in sync.

This assessment covers the VALUE side only, as scoped. I did not re-verify the incumbent's 157 TypeScript errors, the 38% discard rate, or the 5,437 rejected reasoning edges — I confirmed only that no FCDP implementation exists in claudeflow-testing. A complete decision needs the cost side of decommissioning the incumbent compiler, which was not my scope.

Read-only inspection of both repos on 2026-07-29: git history and branch/remote topology in both; the four prior archon port/handoff/validation documents; the pre-existing corpus-index→archon migration spec; live archon binary (1.3.11, 7b44c665) read-only subcommands; quote_verify.rs / archon-draft / archon-docs schema source; compile-corpus-index.py; live npx tsc --noEmit; dissertation drafting file mtimes. No writes, no builds, no pushes.
result.summary:
The strongest case against archon-first does not rest on Rust being worse. It rests on four verified facts.

First, a build-ready, adversarially-reviewed spec for this exact port already exists and has produced nothing. `plans/archon-corpus-index-migration-spec.md` (2026-06-24) specs corpus/index → archon Cozo across nine phases and was endorsed "high confidence." Thirty-five days later `grep -rn 'corpus_entries|corpus_concepts|ensure_corpus_schema' crates/` returns empty and archon's 942 MB store holds 227 documents, all PDFs, zero index entries. The spec's own framing is the decisive line: "The substrate is the easy part; ADAPTER COVERAGE is the long pole. The build is gated not by CozoDB mechanics (verified trivial) but by the heterogeneity of ~19 hand-authored entries." Cozo and Rust buy nothing on the critical path; the long pole is irregular hand-authored markdown, which is where Rust is slowest and where the 231-agent review explicitly recommended KEEPING the five Python parsers.

Second, the two-repo split is not a hypothetical cost — it has already happened and already silently lost data. `archon-cli/index/` is a checked-in duplicate of `corpus/index/` (1,731 tracked files). It is missing three entire entries — Presence Theory (Foundations), Rhetoric of Interactivity and VR (Part III), Social Presence in Virtual Worlds (Part III), 25 files — and its `compiled-index.json` is 643,548 bytes from Jul 16 against the incumbent's 664,494 from Jul 20, different md5. Sync is manual (`chore(index): commit compiled research index as a working data asset`). Archon-first makes the authoring side permanently remote from the compiler.

Third, archon has no delivery capacity and a poor completion record. HEAD 8758f2fa is on no remote at all — `git branch -r --contains` returns empty — with 186 commits unlanded and origin/main frozen since 2026-06-13. Last archon commit was 2026-07-18, eleven days ago. Meanwhile dissertation drafting ran 26 files on 07-29 and 6 on 07-28. Port #2 was declared COMPLETE on 06-25, then an adversarial review found 21 defects (17 confirmed, 7 substantive, including a byte-vs-code-point token estimator that shifted every chunk boundary on the Greek corpus), and a five-item queue was still open on 07-01. The comparable V-3/V-4 quote matcher, scoped "M–L," took 7 commits across 15 days and is still incomplete on three axes.

Fourth, the cheapest thing that works is genuinely days, not months, and the usual justification for porting does not survive inspection. `npx tsc --noEmit` does report 157 errors — but zero of them are in the four index-consuming modules; they are concentrated in section-orchestrator (26) and __experimental__ (45). The index layer being overhauled is type-clean. The highest-value fixes are tiny: reordering two elif arms at compile-corpus-index.py:718-721 kills the pollution that has one centralityTier holding 10,009 chars; adding "index" to three SKIP_DIRS sets stops 518 index manifest records being re-embedded; and adding char_start/char_end to QuoteFragment is a four-line change because local_range is already in scope at quote_verify.rs:371 and thrown away at :405.

The honest caveat: archon's capabilities are real. doc_chunk_blocks carries char offsets, quote_verify resolves sub-span page and bbox, archon-evidence/index.rs is 977 working lines. But archon-draft — where the drafting protocol actually pulls quotations — has no dependency on archon-docs and therefore cannot call locate_quote at all. Two components in the same repo, still unconnected after 15 days of work. That argues for calling archon as a verification service from the incumbent, not for relocating the overhaul into it.

BASIS 1 — the repo's own build-ready spec. `plans/archon-corpus-index-migration-spec.md:130-142` sizes this exact migration at nine phases: P0=M, P0.5=L, P1=L, P2=M, P3=L, P4=M, P5=XL, P6=M, P7=M — one XL, three L, five M. If the cheap-fix path is chosen and then not actually executed, the incumbent degrades further while archon also stalls — the worst outcome of the three.

It extrapolates from one comparable feature (V-3/V-4 at 15 days for an M–L item) and from a spec whose T-shirt sizes were never calibrated against delivered work. If the index overhaul's end state truly requires clause-level character anchoring for ~450,000 clause records, the incumbent must eventually acquire what archon already has. My position is that this is bought by calling archon as a verification service, not by relocating the compiler — but a reviewer who weights the end state more heavily than the transition cost could reasonably reach the opposite verdict.

The 186-commit unpushed backlog is a shared risk, not purely an argument against archon. That work is unbacked-up beyond the local disk (HEAD is on no remote), so an archon-first decision at least creates pressure to land it. Continued incumbent-first work leaves it stranded indefinitely.

Reading the sync-drift evidence as purely anti-archon would be unfair: archon tracks 1,731 index files in git while the incumbent tracks only 335 of 1,759 on disk (1,424 untracked, not ignored — .gitignore has no corpus/index rule). Archon's copy is stale but better version-controlled. The honest reading is that NEITHER copy is authoritative, which is itself the argument against adding a second compiler to the split.

result.port_cost: Two separable pieces, sized against measured prior work in this repo. (1) The parts that already exist need no port at all: the clause layer, the verification gate and the index reader are shipped, merged into HEAD and CI-tested; exposing the offsets is ~25-40 lines (P19). (2) The compiler/authoring adapter has no Rust counterpart and must be built: ~1,900 lines of source to replace (~1,100 of compile-corpus-index.py's 1,412 plus ~600 of cross-author-utils.ts and 202 of corpus-index-provider.ts). Basis for the expansion factor: the FCDP port removed 891 lines of Python across 7 files (365be93b) and added 2,497 lines of Rust including tests and fixtures (8bfe441d), both landed 2026-07-08 alongside the crate scaffold f8779fd1 — 2.8x lines, ~1 day. That projects to ~4,500-5,500 Rust lines for the compiler, i.e. one crate of roughly archon-evidence's size. Basis for the schedule: archon-evidence itself went from crate creation (c98aca59, 2026-07-10) to hardened-and-committed (2bf98d8a, 2026-07-14) — 3,112 lines of crate source plus 2,619 lines of bin modules plus TUI screens, 56 tests, in 5 days. archon-lanham (2,461 lines) was ported in a comparable window (f637a00c, 2026-06-25). So: compiler port ≈ 1-2 weeks at the observed pace, plus the CozoDB record schema and validator (~600-900 lines, ~3-5 days). The ~40-field CLAIM model, the five sibling record types and the migration of ~5,000 authored records are NOT port cost — they are new construction that costs the same in either repo. The genuine archon-vs-claudeflow differential is therefore the compiler (a real net cost in archon) against the corpus store, addressing, verification gate, tested index reader and CI (all real net costs in claudeflow, and one of them — re-ingesting 226 PDFs to recover per-block char offsets and bboxes — is by far the largest single item on either side).
risks: archon has NO index compiler and its copy of the 27 authored entries has already drifted from claudeflow's (2,226 vs 1,856 files; compiled-index.json 670 nodes/2026-07-16 vs 701/2026-07-20). Today's arrangement — compile in Python, hand-copy, consume in Rust — is itself the defect. An archon-first plan that does not fix the sync direction will reproduce this drift at claim scale, where it will be far harder to detect.

HEAD is 186 commits ahead of origin/main and contained by no remote branch (`git branch -r --contains HEAD` is empty). The entire evidence-curation crate, all six critical fixes and the reranker work exist only on this WSL box. Betting the index overhaul on archon concentrates more unbacked value on one machine; the standing rule is push-from-WSL-only and ask-before-every-push, so this is a policy consequence, not an oversight — but it is a real risk to name.

`archon pipeline run <spec>` is still non-functional (src/command/pipeline_declarative.rs:22-23, unchanged since 2026-05-08), so a 224-document extraction cannot be orchestrated declaratively inside archon today. Any bulk authoring run needs an external driver or `archon chat`/`archon coder` until an executor is wired.

The CLI's headline `found` field is unsafe as a gate: REPORT_FLOOR = 0.60 means a fabricated quotation returns `found: true` with fuzzy hits on unrelated books — verified live (Morton, *Ecology Without Nature*, sim 0.725, for the De Anima string). verify.rs keys correctly on match_kind; docs.rs:141 does not. Every new consumer must be written against match_kind, and that discipline is not enforced by a type today.

crates/archon-knowledge is a trap disguised as a head start. Its schema and CLI look like the target, but claim_extractor.rs is a naive sentence-splitter with no locus and contradiction_scanner.rs is an unindexed O(n^2) all-pairs loop that loads every claim into memory. Adopting it unexamined at 45,000 claims (~1e9 comparisons) or 450,000 clause records (~1e11) would fail late and expensively.

Iteration cost. archon-cli is a 39-crate workspace whose CI needs CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 and a 60-second heartbeat loop to survive the runner's memory and no-output limits (.github/workflows/ci.yml:165-197), and local `cargo test` on this box is under a --test-threads=2 rule after prior OOM crashes. A record schema that will churn heavily during authoring iterates faster in Python than in a Rust workspace of this size — that is a genuine argument for keeping the five markdown parsers in Python as an adapter emitting a typed intermediate, exactly as the review recommended, rather than porting them.

Nothing in archon persists a curated claim today, so there is no migration target yet and no precedent for the write path. The first record written to the store will be the first time this system has ever stored a claim; the pack format (pack.rs:117-151) is a file-based handoff, not a store, and its Verification field is a date rather than a content check.
result.summary: The evidence-curation work is real, shipped, merged and tested — it is not a prototype. `archon evidence curate` today runs an agentic research assistant that may only select retrieved spans by id, then produces two files: pack.json and quotes.json. Its record shape is quote-centric — QuoteIndexEntry {id, source, locus, description, intended_use} joined positionally to QuoteEntry {text, cite} and EvidenceItem {id, grade, content}. Something already resembles a claim record with a locus: ReviewItem (crates/archon-tui/src/screens/evidence_curation_util.rs:62-91) carries a one-line claim, a locus, a cite, page, bbox, chunk_id and every located page-box — but it is transient, and NOTHING from a curation is ever written to the store. verify.rs re-verifies each bank quote against the live corpus scoped to the document the pack cites, classifies it Exact/NearVerbatim/Drift/Missing/WrongSource, and blocks every non-exact status. On the 2026-07-13 review: all six CRITICALs are fixed and on the current branch — CR-1/CR-2 by an exact-only delete/reprocess resolver with --all-matching opt-in and two named regression tests, CR-3 by source-scoped verify_bank plus the WrongSource class, CR-4 by gating the 2-up remap on a genuine-2-up check, CR-5 by reading manifest.vector_count in snapshot_is_current plus snapshot invalidation and auto-rebuild, CR-6 by replacing the sticky latch with an expiring cooldown. feat/evidence-curation (2bf98d8a) is an ancestor of HEAD 8758f2fa, so none of this is stranded. The separate "declarative pipeline run non-functional" finding is STILL TRUE and untouched since 2026-05-08. On the sizing question: roughly the clause layer, the addressing, the verification gate and a tested index reader are already built in archon — the corpus is live at 226 documents / 17,824 chunks with per-block char offsets and bboxes, while claudeflow's .archon is 28 KB and empty. What is NOT built in archon is the whole authoring side: no index compiler exists there at all (its index/ is a hand-copied, already-drifted snapshot), no claim/clause/edge/tension/term/source relations exist, no validator, and no persistence for anything a curation produces. That splits cleanly: everything downstream of the record already favours archon and would have to be rebuilt or re-ingested to move to claudeflow; everything upstream of the record is a genuine net cost in archon, estimated at one crate of archon-evidence's size (~4,500-5,500 Rust lines, 1-2 weeks at this repo's measured pace). The honest recommendation the evidence supports is archon-first for the store, schema, addressing and verification, with the five markdown parsers kept where the review put them — as adapters emitting a typed intermediate — rather than ported wholesale.

result.summary: Archon-as-producer is a real migration path, not wishful thinking — but for a reason sharper than "Rust is better". The compiled artifact's three fatal absences (no id, no page, no quote/locus on any node) are exactly the three things archon already computes and already discards. quote_verify.rs computes char offsets (a,b) at line 163-166, narrows page through doc_chunk_page_breaks and bbox through doc_chunk_blocks, resolves a Bekker/PageNumber locator off the running head — then throws the offsets away because QuoteFragment has no field for them. Exposing them is a 2-field change across 4 files, ~10 added lines, with the values already in scope at the construction site. Meanwhile the incumbent compiler ignores 12 structured *-ontology.json files that ALREADY carry canonical_id, page_anchors{unit, book_page}, tier, type, and an explicit `positions` array of claim records — i.e. the id/page/claim layer the artifact lacks is sitting on disk unread. A Rust producer that reads those 12 JSON files and grounds each claim through the existing find_fragment_bboxes gets id + exact char span + page + bbox + locator + match_kind per claim, which no amount of work on the Python scraper can produce because the Python discards offsets in the first statement of every parser and has no corpus text at all. The legacy view is cheap and safe: RawIndex/RawNode/Hook/TensionEdge already model the artifact's 4 arrays; they are missing only 7 optional String fields and the Serialize derive. Two caveats that are real, not cosmetic: (1) the two repos ALREADY hold divergent copies of compiled-index.json today (670/1663 in archon vs 701/1722 in claudeflow-testing, different md5) — archon-as-producer fixes this rather than causing it; (2) the full 45k-claim/450k-clause corpus can never round-trip through the legacy JSON view (~121 MB projected), but it does not need to: the TS renders at most 12 nodes + 3 hooks + 5 tensions per prompt, so the legacy view is correctly a bounded projection.
result.port_cost: ~1,200–1,400 new Rust LOC for the recommended path; ~2,600–3,000 if all markdown scrapers must be ported too. Breakdown with basis: (1) char_start/char_end exposure — 4 files, ~10 lines, values already in scope (measured, see finding). (2) Legacy-view emitter — add `Serialize` + 7 missing fields to the 4 raw structs at index.rs:36-107 (72 lines today) + an emit fn + one CLI arm; basis = the existing verify-quote JSON emitter at src/command/docs.rs:139-165 is 27 lines for a comparable nested shape, and crates/archon-evidence/src/pack.rs already has write_pack as the artifact-writing precedent → ~250 LOC + ~100 LOC golden-file tests. (3) Claim + clause Cozo relations — 2 `ensure_*` fns modeled exactly on schema.rs:193-210 (ensure_doc_chunk_blocks, 18 lines) and schema.rs:215-224 (10 lines) → ~40 LOC schema + ~200 LOC store put/list modeled on store::list_chunk_blocks_for_chunk. (4) Structured-JSON reader for the 12 *-ontology.json files (2 shapes: book-level with concepts/dimensions/positions/notable_tensions, cluster with nodes) → serde structs + mapper, ~400-600 LOC. (5) Claim-grounding driver (claim text → find_fragment_bboxes → persist span) → ~200-300 LOC; basis = crates/archon-evidence/src/lib.rs:362 already performs exactly this locate-and-join for candidates. EXCLUDED and separately estimated: porting the 5 markdown parsers, compile-corpus-index.py lines 195-1176 = ~980 Python lines across 7 layouts → ~1,300-1,600 Rust LOC. That last figure is my weakest estimate: there is no comparable Python→Rust port already in the repo to calibrate the ratio against, so I am applying a generic 1.3-1.6x and flagging it as such. Note the 15 entry dirs with no structured JSON would need this path (or new authored JSON) to reach parity.

risks: The producer front end is the real cost and the structured-JSON path only covers 12 of 27 entry dirs. The other 15 need either the ~1,300-1,600 LOC markdown-scraper port or newly authored structured JSON. Deciding which is the single biggest scoping question, and my scraper-port estimate is the weakest number in this report (generic 1.3-1.6x Python→Rust ratio, no in-repo port to calibrate against).

'45,000 claims' is not achievable from archon's current claim_extractor (crates/archon-knowledge/src/claim_extractor.rs:48-90 is a copula/verb keyword matcher with no offsets). It needs an LLM extraction pass (~400-800 LOC, precedent exists in src/command/curate_agent.rs) or must be sourced entirely from hand-authored `positions` arrays — which today total 18 claims in one file, not 45,000. Do not let the schema work disguise this gap.

REPORT_FLOOR = 0.60 (quote_verify.rs:20) plus `"found": !locations.is_empty()` (docs.rs:142) means a fabricated claim grounds successfully at the API level. Every gate in the claim layer must key on match_kind == Exact. This is the same failure mode as the ped-sec-29 fabricated quotation.

doc_chunk_blocks columns are named char_start/char_end but hold BYTE offsets (schema.rs:189-192), while quote_verify normalizes into a CHAR vector at :150. A claim/clause record that inherits the name without the semantics will mis-slice every Greek, German or accented span — precisely the corpus this index is for.

The exact-FTS path currently errors out on index-expanded queries containing hyphenated canonical terms (reproduced live with 'being-at-work'). A bigger index means more hyphenated aliases and more of these failures; fix before scaling, not after.

The legacy view is inherently lossy — it cannot carry char spans, bboxes, match_kind or clause records at 45k/450k scale (~121 MB projected). That is architecturally correct given the TS caps of 12/3/5 records per prompt, but it must be stated explicitly in the design or someone will later 'fix' the projection by widening it and blow up the loader.

hook.bridge / sourceText / targetText are rendered into the prompt (corpus-index-provider.ts:132,140-143) but are NOT in archon's Hook struct. A producer that emits only what it currently parses degrades every hook line silently — no error, no test, no CI. The golden-file round-trip test is not optional.

The known runtime defects on the TS side (the t.includes('') matcher at cross-author-utils.ts:473-474 firing 31 of 72 hooks for every topic, the '? (Unknown) ... both authors MUST be cited' prompt, the _hooksDerivationDone one-shot at cross-author-utils.ts:54) live in the CONSUMER and survive a producer swap untouched. Making archon the producer improves the data but does not fix the matcher; scope one of the two, not neither.

Standing rules apply to the whole path: back up before changes, WSL-only commits/pushes, ask before every push, and wait for sign-off with evidence before committing. Both repos currently have dirty working trees and archon-cli sits on feat/wraith-retrieval, not main.

result.scope: Storage-layer feasibility for the corpus-index overhaul: can the archon-cli CozoDB store hold ~45,000 claim + ~450,000 clause records with exact provenance? Read crates/archon-docs/src/schema.rs in full and crates/archon-cozo/ to establish every declared relation, the storage engine, indexing, FTS and vector support; measure the live 987 MB store read-only; confirm doc_chunk_blocks actually has rows by tracing quote_verify.rs fragment_for(); project to 450,000 clause records and compare against the incumbent's measured ceilings. Read-only throughout — no builds, no writes, no git write operations.
result.summary:
The CozoDB store can hold the target volume with room to spare, and — more decisively — it already holds the one thing the overhaul is actually about: exact character-level provenance. Verified: the store is a single SQLite table `cozo(k BLOB primary key, v BLOB)` (cozo-ce 0.7.13-alpha.3, features storage-sqlite), 2,751,189 rows / 987,086,848 bytes / 240,988 pages, page_size 4096, journal_mode DELETE, freelist 0. I decoded the Cozo catalogue (relation id 0, 27 rows) and mapped every relation id to its row count. doc_chunk_blocks IS populated: 114,612 rows / 26,360,674 bytes (230 B/row); doc_chunk_page_breaks 27,227 rows; doc_chunk_hashes 17,819; doc_chunk_spatial 11,311; doc_locators 2,961; doc_chunks 17,824 / 56,023,036 bytes of content; the FTS inverted index 2,475,077 rows / 465,776,028 bytes. The sub-span bbox is real and block-driven: `archon docs verify-quote "the soul is in a way all existing things"` returns EXACT, p.48, bbox [66,327,360,368] (41pt tall) with locator 431b1 (Bekker), while the two fuzzy hits fall back to full-chunk boxes 519pt and 472pt tall — exactly the fragment_for() branch at quote_verify.rs:373-394, which calls store::list_chunk_blocks_for_chunk (quote_verify.rs:377) and narrows via sub_span_bbox (quote_verify.rs:343-361) only when blocks are non-empty.

Adding 45,000 claims + 450,000 clauses is a +18% row-count increase (2.75M -> ~3.25M) and, at doc_locators' measured 232 B/row for a text-bearing record scaled to ~450-550 B for a claim/clause row, roughly +200-260 MB on a 987 MB store. That is not close to any engine limit. SQLite's own ceiling is 281 TB; the measured full-scan rate on this machine is ~31M key-rows/s (2,475,077 rows in 80 ms; 114,612 in 3.84 ms), a point lookup is 0.07 ms and a prefix range scan of 2,399 rows is 0.19 ms. Crucially, my probe used the exact SQL Cozo's sqlite backend issues — cozo-ce-0.7.13-alpha.3/src/storage/sqlite.rs:131-139 defines QUERIES as `select v from cozo where k = ?`, `select k, v from cozo where k >= ? and k < ? order by k`, `select count(*) from cozo where k >= ? and k < ?` — so these are the storage primitives, not analogues.

Against that, the incumbent format cannot hold the target at all. corpus/index/compiled-index.json is 666,303 bytes for 2,559 records: ontologyNodes 701 at 649 B/record, crossPipelineHooks 72 at 533 B, tensionEdges 64 at 682 B, canonicalTerms 1,722 at 27 B — and those 649-byte node records carry no id, page, quote or locus. 450,000 clause records with provenance at >=650 B/record is ~292 MB in one file, loaded by src/god-agent/shared/jsonl-loaders.ts:210-211 as `readFileSync(indexPath, 'utf-8')` then `JSON.parse(raw)` into a module-level cache — a whole-file JS string plus a parsed object graph typically 5-10x the text, in every tsx process. That is ~18x past the review's measured 24.97x loader ceiling (~16.6 MB), before the 157 tsc errors and zero tests are considered.

The archon side is not free of defects, but every one is implementation-level and fixable inside the repo, whereas the incumbent's are format-level. The important one: Cozo's StoredRA::iter (query/ra.rs:1502-1509) is `self.storage.scan_all(tx)` plus a post-filter, with no compute_bounds — compute_bounds appears only inside prefix_join (ra.rs:1348). And compile.rs:601 turns `chunk_id = $cid` into `ret.filter(build_equate(...))` when chunk_id is already bound by the preceding atom. So archon's standard query form `*doc_chunk_blocks{...}, chunk_id = $cid` (store.rs:554-556) is a FULL RELATION SCAN today, and there are 24 such `= $param` filter lines in archon-docs/src/store.rs alone. At 114,612 rows that costs single-digit ms and nobody noticed; at 450,000 clause rows / ~200 MB it becomes ~50 ms warm per lookup and far worse cold. The engine has the fast path — scan_bounded_prefix, measured at 0.19 ms — archon's query style just does not reach it. Second: archon-knowledge/src/store.rs:77-87 issues one db.run_script per claim, and with journal_mode=DELETE and no synchronous pragma that is one fsync-bounded transaction per row; 45,000 claims would be 45,000 transactions. archon-docs already has the correct batched pattern (store.rs:508-545, one multi-row `:put` over `$rows`). Third: archon-knowledge has no archon-cozo dependency and makes 7 raw db.run_script calls, so its writes bypass the retry/lock guard that every archon-docs write goes through (cozo_retry.rs:20-28).

The decisive asymmetry is not capacity, it is that archon already computes the offsets the goal requires and merely fails to persist them, while the incumbent never has them at all. quote_verify.rs:162-166 computes (a,b) via find_subslice, local_span_in_chunk (quote_verify.rs:297-311) computes (lo,hi), both are used to narrow page and bbox, and then QuoteFragment (quote_verify.rs:32-42) has no field to carry them. Adding two usize fields there is a smaller change than any part of the incumbent's replacement, and it lands on a store that already has 114,612 block rows to anchor against.

NOT included and identical in either repo: the semantic quality of extraction, and the reingest needed to lift spatial coverage above 63.5%. Storage cost of the result: ~200-260 MB added to a 987 MB store (basis: doc_locators measures 232 B/row for a text-bearing record; a kb_claims-shaped row with provenance columns is ~450-550 B; 495,000 rows x ~500 B), taking row count from 2,751,189 to ~3.25M — a +18% increase on a store whose largest relation full-scans in 80 ms.
risks: Query-form regression is the real scale ceiling, not the engine. Cozo's StoredRA::iter (query/ra.rs:1502-1509) is scan_all + post-filter with no compute_bounds, and compile.rs:601 lowers `chunk_id = $cid` to exactly that post-filter. All 24 `= $param` sites in archon-docs/src/store.rs are therefore full relation scans. At 114,612 rows this costs 3.84 ms and nobody noticed; at 450,000 clause rows / ~200 MB it becomes ~50 ms warm per lookup, in a per-fragment loop, and far worse cold. If the overhaul lands without rewriting these queries it will be slower than the incumbent on lookup-heavy paths despite having better data.

Write throughput under journal_mode=DELETE. The store is not in WAL mode (pragma journal_mode -> delete), cozo's sqlite backend sets no synchronous pragma, takes a ShardedLock write guard per transact (storage/sqlite.rs:76-80) and documents 'only a single writer' (sqlite.rs:34). archon-knowledge/src/store.rs:77-87 then issues one transaction per claim. 495,000 single-row transactions is an fsync-per-row workload measured in tens of minutes, and it blocks all readers for the duration. Must batch before first population.

Unguarded writes. archon-knowledge has no archon-cozo dependency and 7 raw db.run_script calls, so its writes bypass the process mutex, fd lock and 90-attempt SQLITE_BUSY retry that every archon-docs write goes through (archon-cozo/src/lib.rs:119-131, archon-docs/src/cozo_retry.rs:20-28). Running `archon kb process` while an ingest or index-daemon is live will fail hard.

Cozo has no ALTER. schema.rs's run_create (:45-66) only swallows 'already exists'; there is no column-add path anywhere in the workspace. Getting the claim/clause column set wrong means create-new + copy + swap over 450,000 rows later. kb_* relations are empty in the live store TODAY, so the window to get this right is now.

No secondary indexes exist anywhere in archon (`::index create` -> 0 hits). doc_locators already demonstrates the problem: keyed by locator_id, queried by document_id (store.rs:766), unfixable by query rewrite. Any claim/clause access pattern keyed on document_id, canonical term or relation type will need an index whose behaviour is unproven in this codebase.

CORRECTION to the premise: this is not a corpus-wide citation-grade locus. result.summary: Archon-first is the right call, but for a narrower reason than "Rust is better": the overhaul is fundamentally a STORE-and-PROVENANCE problem, and archon is the only one of the two repos that has a store or provenance at all. Measured: archon runs a 987 MB CozoDB with 226 documents / 17,824 chunks / 17,744 pages, all 17,824 indexed (`archon docs status`), with `doc_chunk_blocks{char_start,char_end,page,x0,y0,x1,y1}` and `doc_locators{kind,value,bbox}` declared at crates/archon-docs/src/schema.rs:196-241, and a live quote-verify that returns exact/p.48/bbox [66,327,360,368]/Bekker 431b1 for a real quotation. The incumbent's entire index runtime is one 664 KB JSON blob read whole-file (src/god-agent/shared/jsonl-loaders.ts:212 `readFileSync` + `JSON.parse`, no streaming) whose 701 ontologyNodes carry zero ids, zero pages, zero quotes (verified by direct enumeration: 0/701 for each). You cannot attach 450,000 clause records with per-clause provenance to a record type that has no id.  Engineering health also favours archon, but less than the raw numbers suggest, and I want the downside stated plainly. archon's advantages are real: 515,197 Rust LOC across 39 crates, 8,131 `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attributes in 1,215 files, five GitHub Actions workflows, a documented clippy remediation that took `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` from 243 findings to 0 with adversarial verification of 47 call sites, and `crates/archon-evidence/src/index.rs` — 977 lines, 13 named semantic tests, already a Rust reader over compiled-index.json implementing canonical-term expansion, tension-pole surfacing and owning-work re-rank, including `substring_inside_a_word_does_not_match`, a regression test for exactly the bug class the TS runtime still ships. Against that: `main` is 186 commits behind HEAD and last moved 2026-06-13, and every workflow triggers only on push/PR to `main` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:4-7), so **not one of those 186 commits has ever been through CI**. Clippy is advisory in CI (`continue-on-error: true`, ci.yml:31); the one blocking gate is `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and the project's own report says ~114 files are not rustfmt-clean — that gate would fail today. The four most recent feature commits (0057412b, 7b44c665, c3719bff, 8758f2fa) added **zero** `#[test]` blocks between them, and the last 60 commits are 55 `fix` / 3 `feat` / 1 `test` / 1 `style`. archon's testing culture is historically strong and currently lapsed.  Where Rust genuinely helps here: the schema (CozoDB `:create` + serde-derived types make the 31 unenforced id prefixes and 645 free-text relation values into enums the compiler checks), the validator (the incumbent has no schema file and no validator anywhere — verified), and exhaustive matching over the tension-shape superset the migration spec already enumerates. Where it genuinely hurts: adapters over irregular text. That work is guess-inspect-adjust against 883 markdown files, 271 CSVs in 65 distinct header dialects, and a dozen JSON shapes, and a REPL beats a compiler at it. Cargo.lock lists 1,061 packages, target/ is 21 GB, and ci.yml budgets 45 min (ubuntu) / ~28.5 min (macOS) for a full-workspace nextest run. My honest recommendation is the split the repo's own 2026-06-24 migration spec already implies: put the store, the schema, the validator and the query surface in archon; let the adapters emit a normalized intermediate and keep them wherever iteration is fastest. Two things must be fixed before any of it starts, or archon-first makes things worse: archon carries its own tracked copy of the index (1,731 files, `index/`) that is already 13 days and 31 nodes stale against the incumbent's, and `main` needs to catch up so CI means something again.

result.reasoning:
The claim has a true factual shell and a false load-bearing inference. I confirmed the shell and refuted the inference on three independent grounds.

WHAT SURVIVES. The spec exists at plans/archon-corpus-index-migration-spec.md, dated 2026-06-24 (line 3), and lines 4-5 do carry "5-agent workflow", "adversarial review", "Verdict: endorse-with-changes, high confidence"; line 1 self-labels "(build-ready)". The named relations are genuinely absent from archon-cli: re-running the check correctly (grep -rnE, plus a full 'corpus_[a-z_]+' enumeration) returns no corpus_entries / corpus_concepts / corpus_tensions / corpus_bridges / ensure_corpus_schema and no reasoning_edges anywhere in crates/ or src/. 2026-06-24 to today is 35 days. So: this specific spec's schema was not built.

REFUTATION 1 — "this exact port" is false; the spec is a different, ~1000x smaller task. The overhaul is every claim and every clause of 224 docs (~45,000 claims, ~450,000 clause records). The spec is "migrate-and-preserve the hand-authored DIA/RODA ontology" (line 3) covering "~19 hand-authored entries" (lines 15, 133). Grepping the spec for the overhaul's defining vocabulary — clause, 45,000, 450,000, 224, char_start, char_end, offset, quote_verify, doc_chunk_blocks — returns ZERO hits; the single 'bbox' hit (line 116) is a parenthetical forward-reference to other work. Its companion report sizes the target at ~172 nodes / ~896 edges across 5 pipelines. A spec for preserving ~700 authored nodes is not a spec for extracting 450,000 clause records, and its non-execution says nothing about the latter.

REFUTATION 2 — "build-ready" is contradicted by the document itself. Line 133 makes P0.5 (census + adapter coverage + CSV dialect normalizer + relation-verb census) an unstarted phase explicitly labelled "L (the long pole)"; line 15 says the build "is gated not by CozoDB mechanics but by the heterogeneity of ~19 hand-authored entries"; line 142 repeats that adapter coverage "is where the data-loss risk and most of the effort live". Line 148 lists six unresolved open items, including that Aristotle/Heidegger edges "live only in .mmd/.svg" and need "a .mmd→CSV pre-pass or hand-authoring". A document whose first phase is "enumerate the entries and work out the adapters" is a scoping document. The claim quotes the self-label and omits the eight lines that retract it.

REFUTATION 3 — the predictor is not archon-specific, so it cannot favour the incumbent. The incumbent has the same record, older, on the same problem: plans/index-system-ab-c-evaluation-plan.md line 3-4 reads "Created: 2026-05-01 / Status: Designed, not yet executed" — 89 days, 2.5x the archon spec's age, incumbent-targeted, and its named execution directory tmp/index-ab-c-evaluation/ does not exist. Base rate: 136 plan documents on disk, only 20 tracked in git — including the archon spec itself, which was never committed. Unimplemented plan documents are this ecosystem's norm, not an archon signal. Symmetrically, the incumbent's own 14 commits in the identical window contain zero overhaul implementation: they are corpus content authoring plus "compiler wiring", i.e. adding entries to the same hand-edited registration dict the review flagged. And src/god-agent/shared/cross-author-utils.ts — which contains the always-true bridge matcher I confirmed at lines 473-474 (t.includes(sourceLower) with sourceLower = '') — has first commit and last commit both d6986c803 2026-04-09: untouched for 111 days. On defect-to-fix, the incumbent's 35-day record is also zero.

REFUTATION 4 — the window's actual content inverts the inference. archon-cli logged 188 commits since 2026-06-24; claudeflow-testing logged 14. Effort ran 13:1 toward archon. It went to the ingestion pipeline and corpus flip (plans/archon-corpus-flip-and-pipeline-test-scope.md, 2026-07-01, treats the full flip as still pending), which completed: `archon docs status` reports 226 ingested, 17,824 chunks, 17,744 pages, 0 failed, 17,824 indexed. That is the prerequisite for the spec's own §6 concept→doc_chunks linkage, which was unsatisfiable when the spec was written. Non-execution here reads as sequencing, not inertia — and the sequence resolved in archon's favour.

REFUTATION 5 — "zero implementation" overstates even within archon. crates/archon-evidence/src/index.rs was created 2026-07-10 (6cd6691a), 16 days AFTER the spec, and hardened twice more (91ddc26b, ab97e220): 977 lines, 14 #[test]s, implementing canonical-term expansion, tension-pole surfacing and owning-work routing — the retrieval semantics of the spec's §4 — over compiled-index.json rather than CozoDB. Index capability did migrate into archon during the window; it took a different substrate than the spec proposed.

METHOD DEFECT. The claim's stated command, grep -rn 'corpus_entries|corpus_concepts|...' without -E, is invalid: in basic regex the pipes are literal, so it returns empty regardless of file contents. Control test: the same BRE form searching for corpus_open_paths (which occurs 15+ times) also returns empty, while -E returns hits. The presented evidence could not have distinguished presence from absence. The conclusion happens to hold — I verified it independently — but it was not established by the command given.

NET. The claim's factual core is true and worth keeping: this spec's CozoDB schema is unbuilt. Its inferential core — that this is "the single best available predictor of an archon-first outcome", bearing FAVOURS-INCUMBENT — is refuted. It measures a plan-writing habit that both repos share equally, applies it to a task the spec does not cover, ignores that archon shipped 188 commits and a completed 226-doc ingest in the same window, and ignores that the incumbent shipped zero overhaul work and zero defect fixes over the same 35 days.

result.reasoning:
REFUTED on the load-bearing half. The claim has two parts; the first is true, the second is false, and the second is the one that carries the argument.

TRUE PART (independently reproduced): archon's CozoDB doc store holds only PDF-derived data. `archon docs list | grep -c 'doc-'` → 227; the same list filtered `grep -viE '\.pdf'` → zero rows; `du -sh .archon/archon-data.db` → 942M. I confirmed this is structural, not incidental: all 26 relations declared in /home/dalton/projects/archon-cli/crates/archon-docs/src/schema.rs are `doc_*` or `vec_*` (doc_sources, doc_chunks, doc_chunk_blocks, doc_locators, vec_text_chunks, …). There is no relation anywhere in that schema that could hold an index entry. `archon docs status` → 227 sources / 17,824 chunks / 17,744 pages, all PDF-derived.

FALSE PART: "the overhaul's subject matter has zero presence in the proposed target." The claim equates "the proposed target" with one subsystem (the CozoDB store) and generalises to the whole repo. The hand-authored analytical layer is present in archon-cli in three independent forms:

1. THE SOURCE ENTRIES ARE COMMITTED IN THE REPO. /home/dalton/projects/archon-cli/index/ is a real directory (not a symlink — `file index` → directory): 26 entry directories, 2,055 files, 45 MB, of which 1,731 are git-tracked. `git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only -- index/ | wc -l` → 1731 on HEAD 8758f2fa, branch feat/wraith-retrieval — so this is NOT an unmerged-branch capability. Added by commits e910839c "chore(index): commit compiled research index as a working data asset" and 37c95f47 "feat(index): register VR Pedagogy Secondary + Boredom clusters". File-type breakdown: 842 .md, 494 .json, 237 .csv, 67 .mmd — i.e. the entry prose, the *-ontology.json files, and the edge CSVs. Compare the incumbent: corpus/index/ = 28 dirs, 1,857 files, 46 MB. It is not a divergent fork: `diff -rq` across four shared directories ("In-Game (Calleja 2011)", "A Grammar of Motives (Burke 1945)", "Heidegger - Being and Time", "Dissertation") returned zero differences.

2. THE COMPILED ARTIFACT IS COMMITTED. index/compiled-index.json, 643,548 bytes, tracked at HEAD.

3. IT IS LIVE AT RUNTIME, NOT DORMANT. I ran the read-only command: `./target/debug/archon evidence find --index --limit 3 "poor in world boredom attunement"` → first line of output: `index: 670 nodes / 1663 canonical terms / 64 tension edges (built 2026-07-16T19:28:33.753792+00:00)`, then `index: 4 concept(s) — Poor in world, State-of-mind, Fundamental attunement, Befindlichkeit / Attunement`, `+terms: weltarm, Befindlichkeit, Grundstimmung, Stimmung …`, `tension T3: attunement ↔ invention`, followed by re-ranked candidates carrying `work-boost 1.00 ★PRIMARY` and `provenance: exact-1.00 (sim 1.00) · bbox ✓`. Canonical-term expansion, tension-pole surfacing and owning-work re-rank all fired against the real 664 KB artifact. CompiledIndex::load is called from six sites: src/command/evidence.rs:154 and :218, src/command/curate.rs:341 and :624, src/command/draft.rs:263, and via src/command/curate_agent.rs:27/80/216.

So the store was simply the wrong place to look. Index entries were never ingestible documents — they are markdown/CSV/JSON authored alongside the code and committed as a data asset, which is exactly how archon carries them. The claim's evidence commands are correct but the inference from them is a subsystem-to-repo generalisation error, the "capability asserted from the wrong artefact" failure in reverse.

WHAT SURVIVES AND SHOULD BE CARRIED FORWARD (narrower, and genuinely FAVOURS-INCUMBENT-ish as a cost, not as a blocker):
(a) The analytical layer is not queryable in archon. It is read whole-file into memory: index.rs:269 does `std::fs::read(p)` then `serde_json::from_slice`. That is the same monolithic-artifact pattern the incumbent has, and it will not carry 45,000 claims × 10 clauses. Archon's advantage for the overhaul is that it HAS a store with char-offset relations (doc_chunk_blocks) to join against — but the index does not use it today. The overhaul in archon would have to add relations, not merely port a parser. That is real work the archon-first case must price.
(b) Duplication/staleness cost, verified: archon's copy is behind the incumbent's. `diff <(ls index/) <(ls .../corpus/index/)` shows three entry directories present in the incumbent and absent from archon — "Presence Theory (Foundations)", "Rhetoric of Interactivity and Virtual Reality (Part III)", "Social Presence in Virtual Worlds (Part III)". Archon's compiled artifact is stamped 2026-07-16 (mtime Jul 16 12:28); the incumbent's was recompiled 2026-07-29 12:08. Two checked-in copies of a 45 MB hand-authored corpus drifting apart is a maintenance liability the archon-first plan must resolve (single source of truth), but drift proves presence, not absence.

Net: the claim as stated is refuted. Its true kernel — "the store has no index relation" — is a design gap to close, and it does not support the conclusion that the subject matter has zero presence in archon.

result.summary:
Yes — build it in archon, but gate the cutover on a byte-level differ, not on tsc.

The consumer surface is far smaller than the repo's size suggests. Eleven live consumers, all funnelling through two loaders, reading a total of 22 distinct fields across four arrays. Ten of the eleven never touch a record shape at all beyond those 22 fields, and the entire artifact is 664 KB of uniform, all-string JSON with zero nulls and one key order. That makes a byte-identical legacy view a genuinely achievable target rather than an aspiration — I pinned the complete contract, including the two sort rules, the array-order tiebreaks, and the emission flags.

Two consumers were missing from the brief: scripts/merge-reasoning-edges.py and scripts/reason/reason_over_knowledge.py. The first matters because it reads node["name"] with a bare subscript — a hard KeyError, the only non-silent failure anywhere in the consumer set.

On the risk question the honest answer cuts both ways, and the popular reading is wrong. The 157 tsc errors are irrelevant here: I checked file by file and not one lands in the index path. Every index module typechecks clean. But that cleanliness is a mirage, because every entry point widens to `any` (`loadCompiledIndex(): any | null`, `parsed as CompiledIndex`, `(index as any).ontologyNodes`) — a cast is not a check, and tsc would not catch a renamed field, a missing field, or a null. Meanwhile there are zero tests across 436 test files, zero CI references, and seven separate silent-catch layers. A malformed archon-emitted file yields a successful run with a quietly smaller prompt: no exception, no log line, no non-zero exit. So: less risky at the type level, considerably more risky at the behavioural level. The swap is safe only with a differ.

Two bug-compatibility landmines will bite anyone who writes a "cleaner" emitter. I verified 31 of 72 hooks have an empty targetConcept, which makes `t.includes("")` always true — those 31 fire for every topic, and filling them in silently changes bridge selection on every run. And the tag ranking tests for the substring "medium" while the live values are INTERP-med — so med and low currently score identically. Normalizing either one is an invisible behaviour change with no test to catch it.

The case for archon is one-sided on substrate rather than on preference. archon holds 987 MB of CozoDB with 226/227 documents, 17,824 chunks and 17,744 pages ingested; claudeflow-testing/.archon is 28 KB and empty. The goal's core requirement — character offsets for 450,000 clause records — already exists as schema (doc_chunk_blocks with char_start/char_end/page/bbox), while the Python compiler contains no positional API that survives into a record: its seven .start() calls are all consumed immediately to slice section boundaries. And archon already reads this exact artifact in 977 tested Rust lines, live. I confirmed the provenance end to end: verify-quote returned exact match, similarity 1.000, p.48, bbox [66,327,360,368], Bekker 431b1.

One finding deserves attention on its own: archon-cli already carries its own copy of the index at index/compiled-index.json, dated 2026-07-16 with 670 nodes / 1663 terms — exactly the incumbent's HEAD, while the incumbent's worktree sits at 701 / 1722 and is uncommitted. Two producers of truth already exist and have already drifted. That is an argument for consolidating, but it also means no diff is meaningful until the baseline is frozen — which is the first step, and it needs a commit decision that is currently an open question in the handoff.

(2) Constant-only rule with no scan: archon-session/src/storage.rs:822 `?[id] := id = $sid`.
(3) HNSW index search — the actual corpus retrieval path: archon-docs/src/retrieval_semantic.rs:159, retrieval_image.rs:58, archon-knowledge/src/hybrid_retriever.rs:159, archon-constellation/src/store.rs:85.
(4) FTS index search: archon-docs/src/retrieval_exact.rs:165.

I could not refute the load-bearing core. All five cited line references are literally accurate, and the "already USES them" half — the part most likely to be a struct-definition fantasy — is confirmed by live measurement, not inference. But the claim is overstated in three ways that matter for a FAVOURS-ARCHON argument, and one of them ("zero acquisition cost") is wrong for the producer scope the claim itself names.

WHAT SURVIVES (all independently verified)

1. The cited lines say what is claimed, verbatim. /home/dalton/projects/archon-cli/crates/archon-docs/src/quote_verify.rs:162-166 is `if let Some(mstart) = find_subslice(&doc.norm.chars, &q) { let (a, b) = (doc.norm.orig_byte[mstart], doc.norm.orig_byte[mstart + q.len()]);`. :237 is `local_span_in_chunk(reconstructed, chunk_index, a, b, chunk_len)` inside the `local_of` closure (:231-238). :249-254 passes `local_of(first).map(|(lo,_)| lo)` / `local_of(last).map(|(_,hi)| hi.saturating_sub(1))` into `sub_span_page`. :391 is `sub_span_bbox(&blocks, page, lo, hi)`. :405-411 constructs `QuoteFragment { chunk_id, page, bbox, coord_space, locator }` — no span field; the struct definition at :32-45 confirms it has no such field.

2. It is NOT a capability asserted from a schema. Measured live: `archon docs verify-quote --json --doc doc-0864cb0d... "Simulation provides a mechanism for 'deliberate practice' in a safe, learning environment."` returns exact/sim 1.0/page 11, bbox [40.45, 271.73, 508.81, 344.61] → height 72.9pt. The same chunk (chunk-...-11) queried with its FULL content returns bbox height 437.5pt and page span 11-12. So the offsets demonstrably narrow both page (11-12 → 11) and bbox (437pt → 73pt). This is a pedagogy PDF, not the Aristotle showcase.

3. Not a one-document fluke. 10 `archon evidence find --mode exact` queries across the corpus yielded 52 distinct documents; 52/52 returned `coord_space: "marker"`, i.e. the doc_chunk_blocks path is broadly populated on the live store.

4. "Purely a missing struct field" is literally true of the named struct. `fragment_for` (:368) already RECEIVES `local_range: Option<(usize, usize)>` as a parameter, and `local_range` is still in scope at the `QuoteFragment` construction at :405. Adding `pub span: Option<(usize,usize)>` plus `span: local_range` is a two-line change with no new computation.

WHAT IS WRONG (corrections, not refutations)

A. "exact char offsets" is wrong twice. `Normalized` is `{ chars, orig_byte }` (:472-475) and :519 pushes `s.len()` as the sentinel — these are BYTE offsets. And they index `Reconstructed.original` (:525-550), a SYNTHETIC concatenation of the doc's chunks joined by '\n' in sort order — not the source document. Only the derived (lo,hi) from `local_span_in_chunk` (:297-311) is a durable anchor: chunk-local BYTE range into `chunk.content`. The free datum is (chunk_id, lo, hi) in bytes, not char offsets into a document.

B. Offsets exist only on the EXACT path. `find_fragment_bboxes` passes `None` for `matched_span` on the fuzzy branch; the parameter doc at :220-222 states it. Demonstrated: the Morton fuzzy hit (sim 0.725) for the Aristotle needle returned bbox [76.73, 58.71, 805.50, 577.79] — whole-page scale — and a `source_span` of the entire ~3,900-char chunk. No offsets, no narrowing.

C. "narrow page and bbox" is BLOCK-granular, contradicting the "Sentence-tight bbox" doc comment at :341. Counter-example measured: the 40-character quote "Presence is a human reaction to immersion" in doc-560fd1a3 chunk-2 returns bbox height 125.35pt — byte-identical to the box returned when the ENTIRE ~4,700-char chunk was the needle. Narrowing is exactly as fine as Marker's block segmentation, which for running prose is the paragraph.

D. "zero acquisition cost" is false for the scope named ("index-reader-to-producer"). This is a reader path: it needs a needle you already have, rebuilds the whole document in memory (`Reconstructed::build` concatenates every chunk, :533-543) and runs a naive O(n·m) window scan (`find_subslice`, :563-568). Measured 0.941s wall for one --doc-scoped lookup (debug build). At the stated sizing of ~450,000 clause records that route is ~117 CPU-hours even assuming a 10x release speedup. The genuinely zero-cost producer route is a different mechanism the claim does not name: `doc_chunk_blocks.char_start/char_end` are already written at ingest (block_chunking.rs:373-395), and clause-level offsets fall out of whatever segmenter creates the clauses.

E. Marker-gated. block_chunking.rs:373 is `if coord_space == COORD_MARKER && !out.blocks.is_empty()` — a poppler/flat-text doc gets no blocks and `fragment_for` (:377-387) falls back to the chunk super_box. Image-OCR/VLM chunks get one synthetic page-break row at offset 0 and no blocks at all (ingest_artifacts.rs:59-72). Empirically this does not bite today (52/52 marker), but "zero cost" holds only for the already-marker-ingested set.

F. Unmerged-branch caveat, which the claim does not disclose. `git cat-file -e main:crates/archon-docs/src/quote_verify.rs` → "exists on disk, but not in 'main'". `git diff --stat main HEAD` shows quote_verify.rs (596), block_chunking.rs (659) and archon-evidence/src/index.rs (977) as pure insertions. main is 186 commits behind HEAD and is a strict ancestor (0 commits HEAD..main), so this is stale-main rather than divergence — the code is real and live on feat/wraith-retrieval, which is what I exercised. But every "archon already has this" statement here is about unmerged feature-branch work.

G. Beyond the one field, downstream plumbing is not free: src/command/docs.rs:151-161 enumerates fragment fields explicitly; archon-draft's `QuoteEntry` (crates/archon-draft/src/lib.rs:169-173) holds only `text` and `cite`; `reanchor_cites` (crates/archon-evidence/src/pack.rs:164-206) discards the entire `QuoteLocation` except page_start/page_end. Carrying an offset to the drafting protocol the user actually writes from is several more edits.

Net: the claim's factual spine holds and is stronger than asserted (live-measured, corpus-wide), but its headline economics are attached to the wrong mechanism. It should be restated before being used as load-bearing.

result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED in substance, REFUTED in mechanism and overstated in framing.

CONFIRMED: `*rel{cols...}, key = $param` with the stored-relation atom first does execute as a full relation scan with a post-filter. I traced the whole path and the outcome is exactly as claimed.

BUT the cited evidence is wrong in three material ways, and the RISK framing is overstated.

(1) WRONG CODE PATH. `StoredRA::iter` (ra.rs:1502-1509) is NOT what runs. `compile_magic_rule_body` seeds `ret = RelAlgebra::unit(...)` (compile.rs:171), so a first-position relation atom always compiles to `ret.join(right, vec![], vec![], span)` (compile.rs:283-284) => `Join{left: Fixed(unit), right: Stored}`. At eval, `InnerJoin::iter` (ra.rs:2171-2189) computes `join_indices = ([], [])`, and `join_is_prefix(&[])` returns TRUE (ra.rs:1512-1520: `indices.into_iter().eq(0..0)` — empty vs empty), so it dispatches to `StoredRA::prefix_join`, not `iter`. The `RelAlgebra::Stored(v) => v.iter(tx)` arm at ra.rs:1911 is unreachable for a rule body because compile never leaves a bare Stored node as the root (`is_unit` is used ONLY in Debug fmt at ra.rs:311 and in `::explain` at db.rs:1026/1060 — never in execution).

(2) WRONG REASON. "compute_bounds is called only at ra.rs:1348 inside prefix_join, which requires a bound left iterator" is false twice over. First, compute_bounds has THREE call sites: ra.rs:1184 (StoredWithValidityRA::prefix_join), ra.rs:1348 (StoredRA::prefix_join), ra.rs:1698 (TempStoreRA::prefix_join). Second, prefix_join does not require a bound left iterator — it is called here with the unit tuple and empty join indices, and compute_bounds at ra.rs:1348 IS evaluated on archon's queries. The real reason there is no pushdown is that `Expr::extract_bound` (src/data/expr.rs:522-604) has arms only for OP_GE/OP_GT, OP_LE/OP_LT and OP_STARTS_WITH, with `_ => ValueRange::default()` at expr.rs:603 — there is NO OP_EQ arm. `Expr::build_equate` builds `op: &OP_EQ` (expr.rs:295-301), so equality filters yield (Null, Bot), the bounded branch at ra.rs:1352-1354 is skipped, and execution falls to `scan_prefix(tx, &[])`. `scan_prefix` with an empty prefix encodes lower=[] / upper=[Bot] over the relation id, i.e. byte-identical range to `scan_all` — so the cost claim lands even though the function named is wrong.

(3) FALSE NEGATIVE GREP. "No body-reordering pass exists" is flatly wrong. `src/query/reorder.rs` is 242 lines of exactly that: `NormalFormInlineRule::convert_to_well_ordered_rule` (reorder.rs:34-242). The `fn reorder` grep missed it because the function is named `convert_to_well_ordered_rule`. The conclusion survives only because that pass is a binding-SAFETY ordering pass: round 1 pushes Relation atoms and const Unifications into `round_1_collected` in encounter order (reorder.rs:40-100) and defers only negations/predicates, so it never hoists `key = $cid` ahead of the relation atom. Right answer, invalid justification.

(4) FRAMING OVERSTATED — Cozo DOES have prefix pushdown and point lookup, and archon already triggers them. `InputRelationApplyAtom::normalize` (logical.rs:297-356) emits a constant argument's unification BEFORE the relation atom (`ret.push(unif)` at line 335, inside the arg loop; the Relation is pushed at 340-354 after the loop), and `convert_named_field_relation` (logical.rs:138-181) fills args in schema key order. So `*rel{chunk_id: $cid, ...}` normalizes to `**0 = $cid, *rel[**0, ...]`, compiles to a join with `right_join_indices = [0]`, `join_is_prefix([0])` = true, and executes `StoredRA::prefix_join` -> `scan_prefix(tx, &[cid])` — a real prefix scan; and for a single-key relation `left_to_prefix_indices.len() >= key_len` routes to `point_lookup_join` -> one `storage.get()` (ra.rs:1261-1332). `$param` is substituted to `Expr::Const` at parse time (parse/expr.rs, `Rule::param`), so `Unification::is_const()` (data/program.rs:1816) holds and the reorder pass keeps it in round 1. Also confirmed `choose_index` (runtime/relation.rs:196-244) cannot rescue the filter form: it only counts `IndexPositionUse::Join` positions, and with nothing bound `cur_prefix_len` is 0 for every index so `chosen` stays None.

(5) "EVERYWHERE" IS ~96%, NOT 100%. In archon-cli: 240 occurrences of the `X = $param` filter form vs 10 of the inline `key: $param` form (e.g. crates/archon-reasoning-quality/src/store/cozo_store.rs:75, crates/archon-completion/src/store.rs:90, crates/archon-cognitive/src/inspection.rs:230). So the fast path is already in the codebase, and the fix for the keyed cases is a mechanical query-string rewrite, not an engine change. Caveat the other way: several hot filters are on NON-key columns (crates/archon-docs/src/store.rs:794 `*doc_chunks{chunk_id, document_id, ...}, document_id = $did` — chunk_id is the key), where reordering alone will not help and a genuine secondary index is required.

NET: the load-bearing sentence is true, so refuted=false. But an implementation decision should not rest on the stated evidence — it names the wrong function, the wrong reason, and asserts the absence of a file that exists. The correct risk statement is "archon's dominant query-authoring pattern defeats an optimizer capability Cozo has", which is a bounded remediation cost, not a store-readiness ceiling. At the overhaul's stated sizing (~450,000 clause records) an uncorrected `key = $param` per-lookup full scan is a real O(N) blowup, so it must be fixed — but I found no evidence it cannot be.

result.corrected_claim: Cozo 0.7.13-alpha.3 executes `*rel{cols...}, key = $param` (relation atom first) as a full relation scan with a post-filter — but not for the reason given. The atom compiles to `Join{left: unit, right: Stored}` (compile.rs:171, 283-284) and eval routes it through `StoredRA::prefix_join`, not `StoredRA::iter`, because `join_is_prefix(&[])` is true (ra.rs:2171-2189, 1512-1520). `compute_bounds` IS reached (ra.rs:1348); it yields no bounds solely because `Expr::extract_bound` (data/expr.rs:522-604) has no OP_EQ arm (`_ => ValueRange::default()`, expr.rs:603), so execution falls to `scan_prefix(tx, &[])`, which is the same byte range as `scan_all`. `choose_index` (relation.rs:196-244) cannot help since nothing is bound. A body-reordering pass DOES exist (src/query/reorder.rs, `convert_to_well_ordered_rule`); it is a binding-safety pass that preserves Relation/const-Unification order, which is why the constant is not hoisted. Crucially, Cozo does support prefix pushdown and point lookup, and archon already triggers them at 10 sites via the inline form: `*rel{key: $param, ...}` normalizes the constant into a unification emitted BEFORE the relation atom (logical.rs:329-354) with args in schema key order (logical.rs:138-181), producing `scan_prefix(tx, &[param])` or, for single-key relations, `point_lookup_join` -> one `storage.get()` (ra.rs:1261-1332). So this is an authoring-pattern debt across ~240 query strings — mechanically fixable and partly already fixed in-repo — not a Cozo store-readiness ceiling. Residual real risk: filters on NON-key columns (e.g. crates/archon-docs/src/store.rs:794, `document_id` on key-`chunk_id` `doc_chunks`) are not fixed by reordering and need genuine secondary indices; at ~450,000 clause records an uncorrected pattern is an O(N)-per-lookup blowup that must be addressed before the overhaul scales.

THE METHODOLOGICAL DEFECT. The cited evidence "claudeflow-testing/.archon is 28 KB and empty" is literally true (32 KB on disk, one 28,672-byte db and a lock file, nothing else) but it measures the wrong thing. It tests whether the incumbent repo contains an *archon* store — which is circular — not whether it contains a provenance store. Pointing at an empty sibling-tool directory while a 6.5 GB HNSW-indexed store with bboxes and Bekker locators sits in the same repo is precisely a comparison against a strawman version of the incumbent.

WHAT SURVIVES. The directional point holds in weakened form, and I confirmed each part: archon's store is larger (226 ingested docs vs 163 distinct doc_ids), fresher (archon-data.db written 2026-07-20, doc-vector-store 2026-07-29, vs knowledge_chunks last write 2026-06-30), far more complete against its own corpus (226/246 = 91.9% vs 163/292 = 55.8%), and its locator extraction is visibly cleaner — archon returns "431b1", while the incumbent's locator field is polluted with truncated garbage values ("02b", "05b", "56b", "03b") alongside valid ones ("1001b26", "1044a7"). Archon also exposes an end-user quote-verification command with exact-vs-fuzzy discrimination; I found no incumbent equivalent surfaced as a command.

CAVEATS I OWE. The prebuilt binary reports 1.3.11 (7b44c665) while archon-cli HEAD is 8758f2fa on branch feat/wraith-retrieval, so the binary was built from a different commit than the checkout — everything I ran reflects 7b44c665, not HEAD. Archon shows 1 source stuck in "Ingesting" and 3 index jobs still running. Archon's PDF image OCR shows 323 failures and VLM 5 failures. None of these refute the store's existence.

So: the claim as written should be rejected and replaced. Deciding archon-first on the grounds that "the incumbent has no provenance store" would rest on a false premise; the honest ground is a maturity and coverage gap between two real stores, plus quality of locator extraction.

It carries a one-line claim (`note`) that the curation FSM REFUSES to skip (evidence_curation.rs:198-201), plus source, collection, a provenance trust string derived from `match_kind`, `page`, `bbox`, `chunk_id`, and `page_boxes` (one page+bbox per bbox-bearing fragment). It is genuinely populated by two production paths — human curation via src/command/curate.rs:44-112 and the agentic RA via curate_agent.rs:454-478 — and a live `archon evidence find` returns exact/1.0 provenance with a real Marker bbox on 10/10 candidates.

Three corrections to the original framing. (1) Its locus is NOT typed: `locus` is a page-only String, "p.N"/"pp.N-M" (curate.rs:34-40,94), and the typed `FragmentLocator {kind: Bekker|PageNumber, value, bbox}` that quote_verify does compute is discarded at this boundary — its only consumers are display paths. (2) It is NOT clause-granular: `text` is the whole retrieved chunk (measured: 679-840 words across all 10 live candidates), clause trimming happens later in pack.rs:92, and the bbox covers only blocks on the span's START page (observed: one 163x8pt line for an 819-word span crossing pp.16-18). It is a CHUNK+CLAIM record with a one-line spatial pin. (3) "Closest in either repo" is axis-dependent, not flat: the incumbent holds 455 persistent {id, locus, text} claim records, 8,623 edge-CSV rows with locus+note, and 235 records with a real verbatim quotation plus a Bekker locus and a rationale (Dissertation/_run-history/*/\_synthesis/master-citation-report-parsed.json) — closer on clause and locus, but wholly unverified (no bbox, no chunk_id, no match_kind), and none of it reaches compiled-index.json, whose 701 nodes carry no id, page, quote, or locus and whose text contains zero quote fields.

It remains transient — the CurationResult travels by temp file that /curate-write deletes (curate.rs:421), and assemble_pack drops chunk_id, bbox, page_boxes and trust, persisting only {text, cite} + {source, locus, description, intended_use}.
